content:
One of the most popular Mac AI transcription apps is getting a major update, with a redesigned transcription editor and significantly improved performance. Here's what's new.

MacWhisper 14 launches

If you haven't heard of MacWhisper, it's an excellent app built by prolific indie developer Jordi Bruin.

It lets users quickly and easily transcribe audio, video, meetings, and system sound on their Mac using local AI models, including OpenAI's Whisper and Nvidia's fast Parakeet.

I use it daily for parts of my podcast production workflow before and after recording, and I can't recommend it enough.

Since MacWhisper's launch in 2023, Bruin has continued to expand features, streamline the experience, and deliver welcome performance improvements.

MacWhisper 14 continues in that direction, with a redesigned editor, faster performance, and a number of other tweaks.

Here's what Bruin shared about the update:

Bruin says that based on early user feedback, MacWhisper 14.1 has already been released, which fixes and refines a number of issues with the new editor. The 14.1 release also adds Gladia as a cloud transcription provider, letting users transcribe with their own Gladia API key.

MacWhisper 14 also includes:

A redesigned AI services screen that's clearer and easier to use. Updated AI models for major providers. A better experience when playing back multiple transcripts at the same time. Improvements to the transcription window, including smoother Cmd+A behavior and real-time editing interactions. Deepgram improvements, including EU/US region selection, filler-word controls, and expanded Nova 3 language support. Cloud transcription uploads that no longer need to load the entire file into memory. Fixes for menu bar positioning, audio/video drag sync, idle CPU usage, and edge cases with meeting recordings.

MacWhisper Pro users can upgrade to version 14 for free. Bruin is currently running a 14% discount for users looking to upgrade to Pro.
